core.text: Hypothesis: remove refresh immediately before every commit while retaining the stipulated row-bound editor. Keep S0 loaded through all three commits; refresh only after editing. Preserve exactly K2, K5 and K7 checked, the other five unchecked, zero incorrect-key writes, read-only scores, final latest-snapshot compliance and the ten-minute ceiling. Do not introduce key-bound commits or mismatch-triggered correction refreshes.

Proposed replay: inspect/select K2 at S0 row 2 in minutes 0-1, commit in 1-2; inspect/select K5 at row 5 in 2-3, commit in 3-4; inspect/select K7 at row 7 in 4-5, commit in 5-6. Refresh in 6-7. Snapshot eligibility advances without changing the loaded S0 rows. The predicted writes are K2, K5 and K7; the final refresh loads S2 and preserves local statuses by key. This construction is prospective, not an observed successful trace.

For a future replay, record action times, loaded snapshots, displayed order, selected rows, intended keys and every actual key/value written. Accept only the exact target status map, zero incorrect-key writes including repaired errors, unchanged source scores, loaded S2 and completion by minute ten. Verify immutable keys after final refresh; score 75 cannot distinguish K5 from K7.

residue.text: The supplied trace establishes one synthetic miswrite after selection followed by refresh. It establishes neither refresh necessity nor recurring mismatch-refresh feedback. Changing/frozen snapshot crossed with row/key binding remains an available future diagnostic; those controls do not replace the deprived workflow in the proposed completion replay.

Claims concern eight invented records only. Real selection binding, detection rates and interruption costs are unknown; concurrency, deletion and load failures are outside the model. Production connectors and human participants are absent. No operational reliability, savings or human benefit follows from the proposed seven-minute result.

tension.account_a: Necessity hypothesis: reliable correction requires a refresh immediately before every commit, even with fixed target keys and final freshness.
tension.account_b: Stable-selection hypothesis: the same valued outcome is possible with row binding when the loaded order remains fixed through every commit and refresh occurs afterward.
tension.prediction_a: On the proposed seven-minute replay, omission of every pre-commit refresh prevents at least one required outcome; final freshness alone cannot rescue correctness.
tension.prediction_b: The same replay writes only K2, K5 and K7, preserves the exact status map, and loads S2 at minute seven. Verified success would falsify the necessity claim within the stipulated model; failure would require examining the logged separating conditions.
